MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MARCH 12, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR MITCHELL at 6:30 p.m. and the City Council convened into closed session in the City
Manager’s Office, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  Zerunyan.

City Staff Present: Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis

CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - EXISTING LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  United States District Court Case No. 2:18-cv-10011-R-MAAx; Cherie Townsend, et al.
  v. Los Angeles County, et al.

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

B.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - EXISTING LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Los Angeles Superior Court Case No. 19TRCV00130; Dr. Hendrik Baars, D.D.S. v.
  SRE DCM PV, LLC; City of Rolling Hills Estates

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one potential cases

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

  ***

MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the Closed Session portion of the meeting at 7:20 p.m.

At 7:27 p.m., MAYOR MITCHELL called the meeting back to order in open session in the City
Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Members of the Rolling Robots Outreach InvenTeam and VEX Robotics Competition Team lead

  COMMERCIAL WINNER: ST. LUKE’S PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH
  RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 2 SILVER SADDLE LANE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 12, 2019
 PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Korey Bradbury, Cal Water provided an update on the status of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Water
Reliability Project.

Paul Moilanen, Hitching Post resident expressed concern regarding traffic safety at the intersection
of Hitching Post and Palos Verdes Drive North, specifically related to the Cal Water Project. Mr.
Bradbury responded to Mr. Moilanen’s concerns. MAYOR MITCHELL suggested that Cal Water
continue to work with the Hitching Post neighborhood to address the concerns.

PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

NONE.

NEW BUSINESS

A.  SECOND MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING – COORDINATED COMPLIANCE
  MONITORING AND REPORTING FOR GREATER HARBOR WATERS TOXIC
  POLLUTANTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the second Memorandum of
  Understanding (MOU) effective April 15, 2019 between the Los Angeles gateway Region
  Integrated Regional Water Management Joint Powers Authority and the Cities of
  Bellflower, Lakewood, Long Beach, paramount, Rancho Palos Verdes, Rolling Hills,
  Rolling Hills Estates, Signal Hill, and Los Angeles, acting by and through its Board of
  Harbor Commissioners, the County of Los Angeles, Los Angeles County Flood Control
  District, and the Port of Long Beach for Administration and Cost Sharing for the
  implementation of the Coordinated Compliance, Monitoring and Reporting Plan for the
  Dominguez Channel and Los Angeles And Long Beach Harbors Waters Toxic Pollutants
  Total Maximum Daily Load.

  Kathleen McGowan, McGowan Consulting provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material) noting that the City’s portion of the cost sharing for this monitoring has
  decreased from $14,546 per year to $6,575 per year. Ms. McGowan further noted that
  the City will also receive a rebate from the first MOU to be credited against the second
  invoice from this second MOU.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Ms. McGowan noted that there have
  been no changes in scope for this project at this time; however, the number of water
  sampling stations may be reduced in the future.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,

  APPROVE THE SECOND MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING EFFECTIVE
  APRIL 15, 2019 BETWEEN THE LOS ANGELES GATEWAY REGION
  INTEGRATED REGIONAL WATER MANAGEMENT JOINT POWERS
  AUTHORITY AND THE CITIES OF BELLFLOWER, LAKEWOOD, LONG BEACH,
  PARAMOUNT, RANCHO PALOS VERDES, ROLLING HILLS, ROLLING HILLS
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 12, 2019
   ESTATES, SIGNAL HILL, AND LOS ANGELES, ACTING BY AND THROUGH ITS
  BOARD OF HARBOR COMMISSIONERS, THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES,
  LOS ANGELES COUNTY FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT AND THE PORT OF
  LONG BEACH FOR ADMINISTRATION AND COST SHARING FOR THE
  IMPLEMENTATION OF THE COORDINATED COMPLIANCE, MONITORING
  AND REPORTING PLAN FOR THE DOMINGUEZ CHANNEL AND LOS
  ANGELES AND LONG BEACH HARBORS WATERS TOXIC POLLUTANTS
  TOTAL MAXIMUM DAILY LOAD.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABENT:  Zerunyan

B.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: REMOVAL OF SIGNS ON PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE NORTH

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the removal of eleven (11) traffic signs,
  which include no stopping or no parking signs, bike route signs and right lane must turn
  right signs; and relocation of one (1) right lane must turn right sign along Palos Verdes
  Drive North as indicated on Exhibit A.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  MAYOR MITCHELL noted that that over the years, many of the signs have become
  redundant.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER HUFF regarding the Walking School Bus Signs along
  Palos Verdes Drive North, Assistant City Manager Gramner noted that those signs were
  not identified for removal as they are still relevant. MAYOR MITCHELL noted the see
  sees many people using the Walking School Bus concept, especially in the afternoon

  Paul Moilanen, Hitching Post addressed the City Council regarding the signage at the
  intersection of Palos Verdes Drive North and Hitching Post/Palos Verdes Drive East.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE REMOVAL OF ELEVEN (11)
  TRAFFIC SIGNS, WHICH INCLUDE NO STOPPING OR NO PARKING SIGNS,
  BIKE ROUTE SIGNS AND RIGHT LANE MUST TURN RIGHT SIGNS; AND
  RELOCATION OF ONE (1) RIGHT LANE MUST TURN RIGHT SIGN ALONG
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AS INDICATED IN EXHIBIT A.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABENT:  Zerunyan

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 12, 2019
 C.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: INSTALLATION OF YELLOW
  FLASHING BEACON ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH IN ADVANCE OF
  DAPPLEGRAY ELEMENTARY SCHOOL

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the installation of a yellow flashing
  beacon for westbound traffic on Palos Verdes Drive North east of Dapplegray Elementary
  School during school start and release times.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE INSTALLATION OF A YELLOW
  FLASHING BEACON FOR WESTBOUND TRAFFIC ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH EAST OF DAPPLEGRAY ELEMENTARY SCHOOL DURING SCHOOL
  START AND RELEASE TIMES.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABENT:  Zerunyan

D.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: RACE AGREEMENT FOR 2019
  HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached agreement with Michael
  Hogue Productions to provide fundraising, promotion and consulting services for the 2019
  Hills Are Alive Race.

  Senior Recreation Leader A-Haja provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the upfront fee paid reltive
  to the total compensation, Community Services Director Clark commented that the
  upfront fee remains the same while the additional compensation varies based on split in
  the revenue from sponsorship and registration.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF’s suggestion that City staff serve as the Master
  of Ceremonies for the event, Community Services Director Clark suggested that staff
  could possibly co-host; but since Mr. Hogue knows many of the sponsors and participants
  it make sense for him to remain involved in that portion of the event.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER HUFF,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE AGREEMENT WITH MICHAEL
  HOGUE PRODUCTIONS TO PROVIDE FUNDRAISING, PROMOTION AND
  CONSULTING SERVICES FOR THE 2019 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABENT:  Zerunyan

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MARCH 12, 2019
 E.  RESOLUTION NO. 2434 ESTABLISHING COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDINATOR,
  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR AND MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT JOB
  CLASSIFICATION, DESCRIPTION AND RESPECTIVE PAY RANGE WITHIN THE
  PROFESSIONAL EMPLOYEE GROUP.

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2434 establishing the
  classification, description and pay range for the Community Services Coordinator,
  Community Services Supervisor and Maintenance Superintendent position within the
  Professional Employee Group.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF regarding additional pension commitments
  resulting from changing one position from part-time to full-time, Assistant to the City
  Manager Davis noted that the part-time position is currently eligible for CalPERS pension.

  Discussion ensued cornering the salary ranges of these position and the cost saving
  associated with these changes.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Assistant to the City Manager Davis
  clarified that the Community Services Coordinator position reports to the Community
  Services Supervisor and both are under the Assistant City Manager.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2434 ESTABLISHING
  COMMUNITY  SERVICES  COORDINATOR,  COMMUNITY  SERVICES
  SUPERVISOR AND MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT JOB CLASSIFICATION,
  DESCRIPTION AND RESPECTIVE PAY RANGE WITHIN THE PROFESSIONAL
  EMPLOYEE GROUP.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABENT:  Zerunyan

City Clerk Luce read the resolution by title.

F.  ORDINANCE NO. 725 – AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CALIFORNIA AMENDING ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 1.12.010 OF CHAPTER 1.12 (ELECTIONS) AND
  ADOPTING PROCEDURES TO CONSOLIDATE THE CITY’S MUNICIPAL ELECTION
  WITH STATEWIDE NOVEMBER ELECTIONS AND EXTENDING THE TERMS OF
